title: Knowing when you are nearly out
target: How your own condition is shown in R.E.P.O. — health, carried charge and a weapon about to run dry — so you act before the warning becomes a loss.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A battery or a charged tool

steps.do: Read your health off the display rather than expecting a number.
steps.because: the player's health display sits on a mesh with a parent of its own and is driven by a colour gradient (PlayerHealth, meshParent, healthMaterialColor)

steps.do: Check which health display you are looking at.
steps.because: the display knows whether it belongs to the menu avatar (isMenuAvatar)

steps.do: Use the sounds as well as the display.
steps.because: being hurt, being healed and being upgraded each have their own sound (hurtOther, healOther, upgradeOther)

steps.do: Read the battery bar's charge and drain as two separate fills.
steps.because: charge and drain have separate fills and values (batteryBarCharge, batteryBarDrain, batteryCharge, batteryDrain)

steps.do: Act on the out-of-battery and needs-charging visuals instead of waiting for the tool to stop.
steps.because: there are visuals for a battery that is out and for one that needs charging, with an effect when a bar is lost (batteryOutVisual, batteryChargeNeededVisual, barLossEffectPrefab)

steps.do: Know that an empty weapon is a state of its own rather than an absence.
steps.because: being out of shots is a state with its own beginning, update and fixed update, and an empty gun has a click of its own (OutOfAmmo, onStateOutOfAmmoStart, onStateOutOfAmmoUpdate, onStateOutOfAmmoFixedUpdate, soundNoAmmoClick)

steps.do: Expect some weapons to build up before they fire, and check what yours puts out.
steps.because: a gun can build up before it fires, with a time for the build-up and a time for the shot, and how many shots it puts out at once, its spread and its range are configured per gun (hasBuildUp, buildUpTime, shootTime, hasOneShot, numberOfBullets, gunRandomSpread, gunRange)

commonMistakes: Waiting for a tool to die instead of watching the bar drain.
Reading the menu avatar's health display as your own.
Pulling the trigger on an empty weapon and taking the click for a jam.
Assuming every weapon fires the moment you press.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
